$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under scripts/ or src/ imports this file.
tranche: M4.2 stage 1 — the MCP surface's ORM register, the transport boundary rule, and three live defects
base: 7e1243fc (v1, after M4.2 P1); mutations run at fe3bb5f0
purpose: This tranche has three kinds of claim and each fails in a different way.
THE REGISTER fails by MEASURING LESS THAN IT SAYS. A scanner that reported 124
sites instead of 153 would be green on every assertion about the sites it did
find, and the whole artifact's value is that the number is complete. So its
mutations are the four ways to under-measure: key the scan on the identifier
`prisma` and lose every transaction-scoped write (M01); drop the schema join and
count `this.byToken.delete(` as a store reach (M02); read every context as
composed and empty the BLOCKED-ON-CONTEXT verdict that is the register's whole
finding (M03); and let a file hold sites with nothing naming what it waits on
(M04, M05). M06 is the artifact itself drifting from the tree.
THE BOUNDARY RULE fails by BEING NARROWER THAN ITS NAME. It is not enough that
it fires on `@prisma/client`: `tenancy-prisma-only` already did. What it has to
catch is the import that names no package — `../shared/database.provider` — and
the whole transport tree rather than one subdirectory (M07, M08, M09).
THE DEFECT FIXES fail by BEING GREEN ON A DOUBLE. Every one of them is about
what PostgreSQL does with a where-clause or a Json value, so each mutation is
run against a REAL PostgreSQL 17 and each restores the exact shape that shipped:
the two coalescing operators (M10, M11), the silent `continue` (M12), the JSON
null (M13), and the five ways the tier-2 chain check can be removed (M14-M19,
procedure: One mutation, one file, one command, run individually and reverted before the
next. Never batched: a batch that goes red says only that something did.
THE DATABASE IS REAL AND IT IS NOT DOCKER. Docker may not run on this laptop, so
the four integration commands run against a throwaway native PostgreSQL 17.10
cluster (Homebrew `postgresql@17`, initdb into a scratch directory, port 55432,
dropped afterwards). Every suite migrates the canonical schema into its own
scratch namespace and drops it, so nothing outlives the run.

commands.gateway-forged: PLATOS_POSTGRES_INTEGRATION_DATABASE_URL=... MCP_FORGED_SCOPE_REQUIRED=1 pnpm --filter platos-agent exec vitest run src/mcp-platform/permission-gateway-forged-scope.integration.test.ts

baseline: Every command above is green at fe3bb5f0 before any mutation is applied: register-test 11/11, arch-test 24/24 (1 pre-existing skip), gateway-unit 12/12, gateway-forged 10/10, macros-postgres 12/12.

mutations.name: M01 the scanner keys on the identifier `prisma` and misses transaction-scoped writes
mutations.guards: the register counts `tx.<model>.<op>` inside `$transaction`, which is where 16 of the 141 delegate sites live
mutations.why: This is the mutation that reproduces the brief's own figure. 124 is what a `prisma.`-keyed scan reports; the tree holds 141 delegate calls and 13 client-level reaches.

mutations.name: M02 the schema join is dropped and any delegate-shaped call counts
mutations.guards: a match is a SCHEMA MODEL paired with a Prisma operation, never a name that looks right
mutations.why: `this.byToken.delete(`, `this.sseSessionAborts.delete(` and `this.toolAclService.upsert(` are all `<x>.<y>.<delegate-op>(` and none is a store reach.

mutations.name: M03 every context is reported composed, so BLOCKED-ON-CONTEXT empties
mutations.guards: the composed set is read off `app.module.ts`'s ComposedContexts literal
mutations.why: 86 of 154 sites are blocked because their owner is not composed. A register that read seventeen composed contexts would report the surface as nearly movable and be wrong about the only thing it exists to say.

mutations.name: M04 a disposition is DELETED, so a file holds ORM sites naming nothing
mutations.guards: every file with a site must name its owning contexts and what it is waiting on
mutations.why: The derived verdict says which of four structural states a site is in; only the disposition says WHICH use case is not on a contract, and that sentence is the whole of 'stop at the call site and name it'.
mutations.note: An earlier form of this mutation emptied the SCRIPT's `undispositioned` list and survived, because the suite carries the same requirement independently. Deleting the row is the mutation that removes the property rather than one of its two guards.

mutations.name: M05 a disposition names a context its sites do not belong to
mutations.guards: a disposition's context list must equal the owners the scan actually found in that file
mutations.why: A prose note nobody joins to the tree goes stale silently. This tranche's own tier-2 fix moved `permission-gateway.service.ts` from two owners to three, and this check is what caught it.

mutations.name: M06 the register is allowed to drift from the committed evidence
mutations.guards: `--check` fails when the tree and docs/audits/win-268-mcp-store-ownership.json disagree

mutations.name: M07 the transport rule loses its `apps/agent` clause
mutations.guards: a transport may not import any module of the deployable the surface is moving out of

mutations.name: M08 the transport rule is deleted entirely
mutations.guards: the indirection `../shared/database.provider`, which names no banned package
mutations.why: The proof asserts BOTH that the new rule fires on that import and that `tenancy-prisma-only` does not, so deleting the new rule is visible rather than masked by the old one.

mutations.name: M09 the transport rule is narrowed to the mcp subdirectory only
mutations.guards: the whole of apps/core-api/src/transports/, not one directory of it
mutations.why: A rule scoped to one subdirectory invites the next surface to be moved one directory sideways.

mutations.name: M10 an unreadable recorded step is replayed with no parameters again
mutations.guards: macros.replay refuses a step with no `params` key instead of dispatching `{}`
mutations.why: THE CARRIED DEFECT, restored exactly. The suite asserts both that the step is reported failed AND that the tool was never called, so a fix that dispatched and relabelled would not pass either.

mutations.name: M11 a non-object params is cast rather than refused
mutations.guards: `row.steps as unknown as MacroStep[]` is a cast over a shape PostgreSQL does not enforce

mutations.name: M12 a refused step is skipped silently instead of reported
mutations.guards: a step that cannot be replayed appears in `results` at its own index
mutations.why: The previous `continue` left `stepCount` at three and `results` at two, so `results.every(r => r.ok)` read as an all-green replay of a macro that ran half of itself.

mutations.name: M13 record_stop sends JSON null for an absent paramSchema again
mutations.guards: the `Macro_paramSchema_json_root` check constraint
mutations.why: Only a real database can report SQLSTATE 23514. The unit suite doubles `prisma.macro.create` with `vi.fn()` and returned the row it was handed.

mutations.name: M14 tier 2 reads the CLAIMED organization again
mutations.guards: nothing — see `declared`

mutations.name: M15 a broken chain abstains instead of refusing
mutations.guards: a forged chain is a tier-2 block, not a null
mutations.why: THE DEFECT ITSELF. `null` meant both 'no policy matches' and 'I could not verify the tenant', and a tier that can only tighten became one that declined to have an opinion.

mutations.name: M16 the three refusal causes collapse to one code
mutations.guards: distinct reasons for a missing environment, a wrong project and a wrong organization
mutations.why: Two guards answering the same code cannot be told apart in an audit line.

mutations.name: M17 the project half of the chain is no longer checked
mutations.guards: all three members of the triple are checked, not two

mutations.name: M18 upsertOrgPolicy stops resolving the scope and writes for the claimed org
mutations.guards: the CRUD helpers are not a cross-tenant WRITE
mutations.why: The suite asserts the refusal AND that no row was created, so a refusal thrown after the write would not pass.

mutations.name: M19 deleteOrgPolicy answers false for a refused scope instead of throwing
mutations.guards: an empty result may not stand in for a refusal
mutations.why: `false` already means 'no such row'. The suite pins both answers in one case so they cannot be conflated.

mutations.name: M20 the unit harness loses its chain double entirely
mutations.guards: the unit suite exercises the chain read at all
mutations.why: Before this tranche the double had NO `environment` delegate, which is why no case in that file could have observed the missing join. An earlier form of this mutation deleted only the assertion and survived; deleting the double is what removes the coverage.

mutations.name: M21 the resolved organization is replaced by the claimed one at its source
mutations.guards: nothing — see `declared`

mutations.name: M22 the environment lookup itself is removed and the chain is assumed real
mutations.guards: a missing environment is a refusal and not a pass

survivors: None. Twenty-two of twenty-four mutations were killed; the two that were not are declared below with the proof that they cannot be killed by anything.
declared: M14 AND M21 ARE PROVABLY EQUIVALENT TO THE CODE THEY REPLACE, and that is a
property of the guard rather than a gap in the suite.
`resolveOrganization` returns `{ ok: true, organizationId }` only after
On every line reachable from that `ok`, the two values are EQUAL. So substituting
one for the other — at the return (M21) or at the where-clause (M14) — changes no
observable behaviour on any input, and no test can distinguish them.
THE CODE STILL READS THE RESOLVED ONE, deliberately. Using the claimed id would
throw the verification away one statement after earning it, and the equality is
an invariant of the current control flow rather than of the type: the day a
fourth branch is added to `resolveOrganization`, the claimed id stops being safe
and nothing would have said so. M22 is the mutation that DOES break that
invariant — it returns `ok` without checking anything — and it is killed.
